titles: DTC Approved? These 3 Benefits Need It (RDSP, CDB, Canada Disability Benefit)
Disability Tax Credit Worth $0? It Unlocks 3 Other Benefits (Canada 2026)
Why Get the Disability Tax Credit If You Pay No Tax? (Canada)
yt.description:
Noah is 10. His disability tax credit saves him $0 on his own return: he pays no tax. So why get it approved? Because DTC approval is the key to three other doors.

Door 1: the Child Disability Benefit. Up to $3,480 a year per child (July 2026 – June 2027), paid with the Canada child benefit; reduced when family net income is over $82,847.
Door 2: an RDSP. For lower-income families, the Canada Disability Savings Bond pays up to $1,000 a year with no contribution (lifetime $20,000). Grants match deposits up to $3,500 a year (lifetime $70,000).
Door 3, at 18: the Canada Disability Benefit. Up to $204.20 a month (July 2026 – June 2027), ages 18–64, income-tested.

The key for all three: CRA approval of form T2201. Then file a tax return every year, even with no income.

Next: the Canada caregiver credit.

Sources: canada.ca (CRA) Child disability benefit; ESDC How much you could get in grants and bonds; Canada Disability Benefit – How much you could receive; Income Tax Act s. 118.3. Maximums; actual amounts depend on income and eligibility. Example family. General information, not advice.

ig.caption:
A tax credit worth $0 can still matter 🔑🇨🇦

Noah is 10 and pays no tax, so his DTC saves him nothing. But approval opens:
1️⃣ Child Disability Benefit: up to $3,480/yr (Jul 2026–Jun 2027), with the CCB
2️⃣ RDSP: bond up to $1,000/yr with no deposit (lower incomes) + grants up to $3,500/yr matching deposits
3️⃣ At 18: Canada Disability Benefit, up to $204.20/month (income-tested)
🔑 The key: CRA approval of form T2201
✅ File a return every year, even with no income
